title: 2017–25 Porsche 718: Many Flavors, Many Price Points
summary: It’s a tough time to be a financially challenged Porsche fan, and I’m afraid I’m speaking from experience. Sometimes it seems as if there are only three distinct collector car markets: Ferrari, Porsche, and The Rest. As the greater market stagnates, P-Cars surge with an average value increase increase of 7.4% for all #2 condition […]
body_text: It’s a tough time to be a financially challenged Porsche fan, and I’m afraid I’m speaking from experience. Sometimes it seems as if there are only three distinct collector car markets: Ferrari, Porsche, and The Rest. As the greater market stagnates , P-Cars surge with an average value increase increase of 7.4% for all #2 condition (Excellent) Porsches in the Hagerty Price Guide over the last 12 months. Remember the days of the $10,000 911 SC ? Das Pfefferidge Farm remembers. As always, assess your Porsche priorities. The carbon fiber, Paint-to-Sample ship has well and truly sailed for limited production and GT Division 911s, but there are still (relative) deals to be found, brand-wide. Transaxle cars— 924s , 944s , 968s , and 928s —remain quite attainable, 914s are a bit stagnant, I doubt 996 Carreras will ever truly be valuable, and folks have yet to wake up to the unbelievable value of highly spec’d, highly depreciated Panameras. And then, there’s always the humble Boxster/Cayman twins. These little cars have always been the salve of the skint Porsche enthusiast, offering exceptional mid-engine balance, a sweet flat-six soundtrack, and that undefinable, inherent Porsche tactility. And somewhere along the way, some 20 years into production, the entry-level Porsche sports car became a serious performer. Porsche AG Even prior to its wholesale discontinuation after the 2025 model year, the collective 2017–25 Porsche 718 Boxster/Cayman model line is considered one of the greatest and most versatile sports cars in history, offering a spectrum between sensible daily and weapons-grade track special. And as one of the newest Porsches in the Hagerty Price Guide, their modestly depreciated status offers value per dollar—just as they did when new. But there were initial doubts. Very much a mid-cycle update to the 2013–16 981-generation despite the internal 982 model designation, the new-for-2017 718 replaced the 981’s sweet suite of naturally aspirated flat-sixes with a pair of turbocharged flat-fours. The hordes were furious, of course, never mind the dramatic spike in power, torque, and performance afforded by turbocharging that extended far beyond the on-paper figures. Porsche AG The base, unappended 718 Cayman / Boxster burbled around with a new 2.0-liter turbocharged flat-four, rated to a healthy 300 hp and 280 lb-ft through your choice of six-speed manual or seven-speed PDK dual-clutch transmission. The 718 S upped displacement to 2.5-liters and output to a meaty 350 hp and 309 lb-ft, supported by the traditional “S” treatment for chassis, drive profiles, and cosmetic accoutrements. It’s true, these MA2 flat-fours aren’t as sonorous or soulful as the 981’s sixers. But for every ounce of lost character they gained five in outright capability and daily tractability; given that Porsche derived these fours from the 911 family’s then-new 9A2 flat-six architecture, it’s no wonder these new grumbly, hot-shot baby Porsches put down 911-esque performance figures. In the hands of Car and Driver testers, a base, PDK-equipped Boxster cracked 0-60 mph in 4.0 seconds flat, 0-100 mph in 9.9 seconds, and the quarter-mile in 12.5 seconds, roundly a dead-match for C&D ’s 991.1 Carrera 4S test. The PDK-fitted 718 Cayman S, meanwhile, matched the prior generation of supercars with a tested 0-60 mph time of 3.6 seconds and a quarter-mile scramble in 12 seconds flat. All this with two very functional trunks and a tested cruising range of 550 miles. It’s my experience that these four-banger 718s make better dailies than weekend treats, and the market generally agrees. Expect to pay between $52,400 and over 100 grand for a base 718 Boxster in #2 condition. That’s a wild swing for a functionally identical car regardless of model year, but since some later model years are still experiencing the natural depreciation curve of a new car, expect values to settle out to total parity over the next decade. Porsche AG Sourcing a base Cayman in matching condition will cost a few grand less, but when you add that spicy little letter “S” to the 718, it flips the script. Condition #2 values for a Boxster S range from $57,000 for a first-year 2017 model to $110K for a 2025. The Cayman S will run several grand more. Some things to consider. Both the 718 Boxster and Boxster S were often ordered as lease-’n-release specials, and thus are not commonly found in “interesting” configurations, Paint-to-Sample (PTS) or otherwise. Caymans are better for bright colors and for manual transmissions, though you’ll pay a premium for both. No performance options available on the base and S are frivolous, with Sport Chrono package, Porsche Active Suspension Management (PASM), and Porsche Torque Vectoring (PTV) considered the trifecta. So, who’s the key demographic here? Gen X takes the cake with 38% of insurance quotes compared to a 31% share of the collector car market as a whole, followed by millennials (29%) and boomers (26%). Gen Z and Preboomers lag at 5% and 1% respectively, but these are both expected based on preboomer’s 4% market share and that Gen Z’s yet to come into true purchasing power. This spread makes sense; there might be occasional rivalry between Boxsters and 911s, but the appeal of a Porsche sports car continues to transcend generations. Porsche In your research, you’ll find two short-lived curios in the 718 family tree, only one of which is currently tracked in the Hagerty Price Guide. The 2020–23 718 T pulls its formula from the modern 991.2/992 Carrera T , keeping the base 2.0-liter engine but adding standard PASM, a limited-slip differential, Carrera wheels, and Sport Chrono package. Cool, but its mere $3000-ish price differential from the 718 S kept production (and interest) low when it came out. You won’t find the T tracked in the price guide at this time, but the relatively forgotten 2018–19 GTS is in there. This is the standard Porsche GTS treatment: uprated suspension, standardized performance hardware (PTV, Sport Chrono), and an extra 15 hp from the 2.5-liter four compared to the S. The interior is often kitted with sport seats, carbon fiber, and Alcantara surfaces, and exterior accent trim is darkened for max tacticool. Brian Makse Great idea, but the end result was that of a slightly hotter S, and not a wholly distinct trim, especially as much of the go-fast hardware was available as an upgrade on said S. Porsche fixed this in spectacular fashion with the subsequent 2020–25 718 GTS 4.0 , effectively the GTS 2.5 but fitted with the thrumming 4.0-liter naturally aspirated flat-six shared with the concurrent Cayman GT4 and Boxster Spyder . Some—myself included—are of the opinion that the GTS 4.0 represents the greatest all-rounder Porsche sports car of at least the past 25 years. It’s genuinely that good; 394 hp and 317 lb-ft is healthy, but it’s how said power is delivered that’ll have you searching for one That 4.0 feels like a heart from yesteryear, howling with a mechanical thrash that’s equal parts metallic zing and snorting intake rush, all the way to its 7800–8000 rpm red line (depending on transmission). Now that’s how you make a special car. Unfortunately for my garage, the market nods along. In condition #2, the GTS 4.0 carries an average value of between $111,250 (Cayman) and $133,000 (Boxster). Again, some of this is driven by the 4.0’s status as a nearly new car, but these special, special cars show signs of appreciation following the recent discontinuation of the entire 718 model lineup after the 2025 model year. Richard Pardon Speaking of appreciation, we’re now moving into a different tier of collector-grade Porsches. The 718 Cayman GT4 and Boxster Spyder are, without pretense, some of the greatest sports cars in automotive history, full stop. Building on the success of the 981-generation cars, Porsche’s famed GT division cut fat and honed nearly every aspect of the 718 for a car that’s equally at home on-track as it is sizzling up the tightest technical canyon road you can source. That 4.0-liter from the GTS returns with just 20 extra hp, but the GT4/Spyder’s additional dynamic athleticism is a meaningful step up over the GTS 4.0’s balance of usability. The near-identical average condition #2 value between Cayman GT4 ($140,750) and Spyder ($138,500) are, in my opinion, a direct result of a tidy supply-and-demand equilibrium achieved by fewer Spyders sold against the fan-favorite GT4. Porsche AG A few considerations. All cars fitted with the 4.0-liter also share the same available six-speed manual transmission that does have rather tall gearing, as everyone and their mother will tell you. At the top of second gear, you’ll merge at near 85 mph, and at the top of third, you’ll streak by that unmarked Charger at 121 mph. These big lungs are a bit at odds with the 718 platform’s compact, backroads vibe, but certainly not a deal breaker in the slightest. The aftermarket stepped up with a readjusted ratio for some of the gears to a great effect—or so I’ve been told—but do plan for a five-figure investment if you chose this path. The better news? The market shows this to be a neutral-to-value-additive modification. The 718 Spyder is a significant step up over the 981-generation Spyder, which was closer to a Boxster GTS with the Carrera S’ 3.8-liter flat-six than a true crop-top Cayman GT4. This time, both GT4 and Spyder share general chassis architecture and raw capability aside from the Spyder’s fair weather preference. The 718 Spyder simplifies some of its predecessors’ manual roof foibles, with the 718’s manual folding canvas top requiring only manual raising and lowering as opposed to complete component removal. Porsche Porsche Porsche Not so with the ultra-hardcore 718 Boxster Spyder RS . While its multi-part fabric roof is best described as “contraption” or “493-hp camping tent,” the 718 RS’ transplanted 911 GT3 (yes, that GT3) 4.0-liter requires higher clearance than the standard Spyder’s top allowed for. Thus, this bimini-style roof triggers a severe warning at and above 125-mph, and is suggested only for emergency downpours and car washing, not as a full-time top. Most owners will likely keep theirs parked in their car cave when the weather is anything but blindingly sunny. A bummer, but this also elevates the Spyder RS to one of the most special and singular driving experiences in modern Porsches; there’s nothing protecting you from either the sound or the fury of that GT3 heart. Porsche Then, there’s the shocking and comprehensively RS-ified Cayman chassis, a significant elevation above the standard GT4 in handling, aero, and feedback. A true Weissach weapon, and one that launched amidst a swell in Porsche speculation; by the time of its introduction in 2022, it was clear a well-specified, properly PTS’d Porsche GTx was your ticket to social media adulation, flipped profit, or both. Orders for the GT4 RS flowed in, with many paying hefty dealer markups for purchase privilege. As such, there’s an impressive amount of special order GT4 RSs with lengthy options lists that are either trading slightly above, at, or below the original MSRP, while low-option cars aren’t too far behind. Values are on the rise. As of now, the average value of a condition #2 GT4 RS sits at $224,000 against the original 2025 model-year MSRP of around $165,000. Meanwhile, the inimitable Spyder RS had one less model year and likely significantly less take rate with an average value of $227,000 against the same original starting price. The so-called “baby Porsche” is clearly a baby no more. While I won’t say there’s a 718 for every budget, there’s certainly a flavor for every preference, and you might want to get yours before values inevitably rise (further) out of reach. For max value, skip the final model years for an earlier car with low-to-medium miles, as they quite literally didn’t change a darn thing between model years aside from adjusting variant availability. Porsche The post 2017–25 Porsche 718: Many Flavors, Many Price Points appeared first on Hagerty Media .

title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports partition-level topology for Slurm orchestrated clusters
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports partition-level topology for Slurm orchestrated clusters
body_text: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports network topology configuration at the partition level for Slurm orchestrated clusters. A single cluster can now run tree topology in one partition and block topology in another, with each partition using the topology best suited to its instance types. This improves distributed training performance by keeping job placement aligned with the interconnect characteristics of each instance type, so GPU-to-GPU communication is faster, NCCL collective operations are more efficient, and training throughput improves. HyperPod determines the topology for each partition based on the instance types of its compute instance groups. Partitions with Amazon EC2 UltraServer instance types such as ml.p6e-gb200.36xlarge use block topology, and those with hierarchical-interconnect instance types such as ml.p5.48xlarge, ml.p5e.48xlarge, and ml.p5en.48xlarge use tree topology, while partitions with instance types that don't provide network topology information remain fully schedulable. HyperPod maintains this configuration automatically as the cluster changes through scale-up, scale-down, and node replacement events, so each partition's topology always reflects the current state of the cluster. To get started, create or update a SageMaker HyperPod Slurm cluster running Slurm 25.11 or later with supported GPU instance types. Topology-aware scheduling is enabled by default and requires no configuration. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker HyperPod is supported. To learn more, see Using topology-aware scheduling in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod .

title: Why Semiconductor Test Infrastructure Matters More Than Ever
summary: Discover why wafer test infrastructure, FormFactor's Texas expansion, and new investments are helping strengthen semiconductor innovation and manufacturing.
body_text: July 8, 2026 As AI, advanced packaging, high-speed communications, and next-generation computing continue to reshape the industry, the ability to test devices accurately and at scale will be just as important as the technologies themselves. The semiconductor industry is experiencing one of the largest periods of investment in its history. New fabrication facilities are being built, advanced packaging capacity is expanding, and governments around the world are investing billions to strengthen domestic semiconductor manufacturing. Yet one essential part of the semiconductor ecosystem doesn’t get nearly as much attention as chip design or wafer fabrication: wafer test. Whether it’s powering an AI processor, a smartphone, or an automotive system, every semiconductor device must be tested before it reaches the market. As AI processors, high-bandwidth memory (HBM), advanced packaging, and automotive electronics continue pushing performance boundaries, wafer test infrastructure has become just as essential as fabrication capacity. Without enough testing capacity, even the world’s most advanced chips can become bottlenecked before they ever reach customers. Wafer Test Is Essential to Semiconductor Manufacturing Before a semiconductor device is packaged, it undergoes wafer test to verify electrical performance and identify defective dies while they are still on the wafer. Testing devices at this stage gives manufacturers valuable insight into yield, process variation, and overall device performance before additional manufacturing costs are incurred. Finding problems early helps reduce manufacturing costs while preventing defective devices from advancing further through production. At the heart of wafer testing are probe cards , which create the electrical connection between automated test equipment (ATE) and each individual die. Probe cards may look straightforward, but they’re highly engineered systems built to deliver consistent electrical contact across thousands of test cycles while meeting increasingly demanding performance requirements. As semiconductor devices continue to become more complex, probe card technology and wafer test capabilities must evolve alongside them. AI and Advanced Packaging Are Raising the Bar Several technology trends are making wafer test significantly more challenging. Artificial intelligence workloads require dramatically higher memory bandwidth and processing performance. Chiplet architectures introduce additional complexity through heterogeneous integration. Advanced packaging technologies continue shrinking interconnect pitches while increasing I/O counts. Each of these innovations creates new challenges for wafer-level testing. Engineers must capture increasingly precise measurements while maintaining throughput and manufacturing efficiency. Probe cards must support finer geometries, higher frequencies, tighter tolerances, and more demanding electrical requirements than ever before. Today, wafer test does far more than verify that a device functions as intended. It plays an important role in optimizing yield, improving reliability, and helping manufacturers bring advanced semiconductor technologies to production at scale. Infrastructure Is More Than Just Buildings When people think about semiconductor infrastructure, they often picture fabrication plants filled with expensive manufacturing equipment. In reality, the semiconductor ecosystem depends on a much broader network that includes: Advanced manufacturing facilities Wafer test and probe card production Engineering and R&D laboratories Specialized equipment suppliers Highly skilled technical workforces Regional supplier ecosystems Together, these capabilities give the industry the foundation it needs to innovate while building a more resilient supply chain. Expanding wafer test capacity is particularly important because every wafer produced ultimately requires testing before devices can move downstream. Public Investment Is Helping Strengthen Domestic Manufacturing Recognizing the strategic importance of semiconductors, federal and state governments have launched initiatives aimed at strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities. But these investments aren’t limited to wafer fabrication. They also encourage expansion across the broader semiconductor supply chain, including design, packaging, materials, equipment, and wafer test infrastructure. Texas has become one of the nation’s fastest-growing semiconductor hubs through investments in manufacturing, workforce development, and advanced technology infrastructure. Programs such as the Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund (TSIF) are designed to encourage projects that expand semiconductor research, manufacturing, and related technologies throughout the state. FormFactor’s Texas Expansion Reflects a Broader Industry Trend A recent example of this momentum is FormFactor’s expansion in Farmers Branch, Texas . The company is establishing a new probe card manufacturing facility that is expected to create more than 600 new jobs while representing approximately $140 million to $170 million in capital investment. In July 2026, Governor Greg Abbott announced that the project would receive a $24.2 million grant through the Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund. According to the Governor’s Office, the investment supports Texas’ continued efforts to strengthen semiconductor manufacturing, expand workforce development, and reinforce domestic supply-chain capabilities. The new facility will manufacture FormFactor’s advanced probe cards used in wafer-level semiconductor testing, helping support growing demand for technologies used across AI, high-performance computing, automotive electronics, communications, and other advanced semiconductor applications. While this marks an important milestone for FormFactor, it also reflects a broader trend across the semiconductor industry. As next-generation devices become more sophisticated, investments in wafer test infrastructure are becoming just as important as investments in fabrication capacity. The Future of Semiconductor Innovation Depends on the Entire Ecosystem Breakthrough semiconductor technologies do not reach customers through design innovation alone. They depend on an ecosystem that can design, manufacture, test, package, and deliver increasingly sophisticated devices at production scale. Investments like FormFactor’s new Texas manufacturing facility show how expanding semiconductor test capacity helps support both innovation and long-term industry growth. In addition to creating hundreds of high-skilled jobs, the new facility strengthens domestic manufacturing capabilities and reinforces the critical role wafer test plays in the semiconductor value chain. As AI, advanced packaging, high-speed communications, and next-generation computing continue to reshape the industry, the ability to test devices accurately and at scale will be just as important as the technologies themselves.

title: My New Journey
summary: Why AI is the translational layer between human and machine, why the software engineer’s role will evolve rather than disappear, and why I joined HappyRobot to build it.
body_text: The other day, I wrote: "Why do we write? Almost everything we do is just a data (energy) transfer." Make a note of this, I’ll come back to this later. To position yourself to capture the value of an ever-evolving landscape, you need to engage in bouts of deep thought, strategic planning, and questioning of your assumptions of the future. There is no single answer; everyone has their own variation of this and adjusts accordingly. For me, that started with questioning what the next phase of our technological landscape will look like: how software will be built, how humans will interact with it, and what role AI will play in the dance between the screen and our thoughts. My three takes: AI is the translational layer between human and machine We must treat AI as a thought partner. A companion that exists with an alternative set of skills and opinions to our own AI will be better than humans at many tasks; humans will be better than AI at many tasks. Where does the intersection of true collaborative work efficiency lie, and how do we get there? I subscribe to the perspective that AI will cause a boom in software jobs. Just, not software jobs as we know them, or knew them. In recent years, software engineers have been evaluated on building with pre-existing languages, atop pre-existing operating systems, atop pre-existing kernels. This new "AI layer" will be no different. The role of the software engineer will not disappear; it will evolve. English is now a programming language. Designing reliable systems will no longer rely on the manual transfer of information from your mind to another language that then needs to be compiled into machine readable data. This process now relies on thought alone, and the implementation, albeit with human led systems and guardrails, will be abstracted away from expressing this keystroke by keystroke. Software veterans might read this and scoff. They might argue understanding of the software and true expertise does not exist without understanding each individual part and process of how the code is organized. To them, I ask: would you like me to walk through hole-electron pair generation in the depletion region of the silicon before I trust my code to run my integer math, or are we only pretending depth matters when the person at the keyboard is forging a path you might not believe exists, because it has yet to be discovered? Then I say: By that logic, no one understands software until they can derive Boolean logic from semiconductor physics, which would disqualify most of those people making that argument. If understanding how to write and build reliable software systems requires ‘true’ full-stack knowledge all the way down to its core, then either explain charge carrier behavior in the depletion region before you merge your next PR, or admit we all work on abstractions we do not fully derive. Generating code is cheap, but implementing usable code touches on the most human quality that will continue to set us apart from AI: social interaction. This will keep AI from "replacing all of our jobsss, ahhhh!!!" but will make us more valuable in areas previously assumed to be worthless, many of which are still being proved out. That is where the future value lies, that is what I want to capture, that is where I will position myself. In today’s market, roles that capture this value sit in the realm of a Forward Deployed Engineer; a role that leans heavily on social interaction and strategy, but also on technical understanding of how to build an AI system that can be useful to another individual or organization. It is a role where we do not build a piece of software and see where it lands, but rather start with a sharp pain point and build backwards to the solution. A unique and fully customized workflow. Dynamically tailored. Obsessively contextual. Ever evolving. This week, I joined HappyRobot. They are not only aligned with this vision, but are actively building it. Unlocking and leaning on the desire of humans to connect, they are building the future software and data infrastructure that lets humans get back to being human. I am so happy to be a part of this journey, to join an incredible team and to start contributing to projects that are shaping the frontier of how AI is utilized in real domains. If you’ve made it this far, thank you for reading. These were my real thoughts and words. Keep Building, Jennings

body_text: Fury Gold Mines Provides Update on Precautionary Evacuation of Eau Claire Camp Due to Nearby Wildfire July 15, 2026 View PDF Version View French Version All personnel safely evacuated; exploration activities temporarily suspended as a precautionary measure TORONTO, Canada – July 15, 2026 – Fury Gold Mines Limited (TSX and NYSE American: FURY) (“ Fury ” or the “ Company “) today announces that, as a precautionary measure, it has evacuated all personnel from its Eau Claire camp, located in the Eeyou Istchee Territory in the James Bay region of Northern Quebec, due to a forest fire burning in the vicinity of the site. The evacuation was carried out in coordination with local authorities and the Company’s emergency response protocols. All employees and contractors have been safely evacuated from the camp, and no injuries have been reported. Exploration and drilling activities at Eau Claire have been temporarily suspended while the situation is assessed. We will continue to monitor conditions closely and will resume activities at site as soon as it is safe to do so.” The Company does not currently expect this precautionary suspension to have a material impact on its previously disclosed Phase 2 drill program at Eau Claire, but will provide a further update once activities resume and the extent of any delay can be assessed. title: Finding a Startup Accounting Service Offering Same-Day Answers on Bookkeeping, Taxes, and Compliance Questions
summary: Finding a Startup Accounting Service Offering Same-Day Answers on Bookkeeping, Taxes, and Compliance Questions
body_text: Specialized virtual accountants for small business and fractional CFO firms typically provide a dedicated Slack channel with a named CPA for same-day answers. However, instead of relying on a dedicated CPA via chat, many founders prefer platforms like Fondo that automate bookkeeping, tax filings, and tax-credit recovery, eliminating the need for constant back-and-forth communication. Introduction Early-stage startups often face complex financial compliance requirements, ranging from multi-state tax obligations to capital management. Managing unstructured financial workflows and looming startup tax season deadlines frequently leads founders to seek out a dedicated CPA available directly in a Slack channel. Choosing the right accounting service requires deciding between this high-touch, human-led advisory model and a scalable, automated platform approach. Founders must determine whether they need continuous chat-based reassurance or a system that quietly handles the work in the background. Key Takeaways Fractional accounting firms offer dedicated, real-time Slack communication for bespoke compliance and tax questions. Automated bookkeeping platforms reduce the manual categorization errors that typically prompt the need for continuous CPA communication. Fondo provides a highly efficient alternative by putting corporate taxes , bookkeeping, and tax-credit recovery on autopilot for startups. Startups must evaluate whether they truly need day-to-day advisory via chat or systemic automation that eliminates repetitive financial tasks altogether. Why This Solution Fits The primary reason founders want same-day answers from a CPA is a lack of visibility into their financial health and impending tax deadlines. Traditional venture-backed accounting models often require constant communication. Founders find themselves regularly logging into portals to categorize transactions, reviewing complex Section 174 capitalization rules , and answering accounting questions just to prepare investor-ready reporting. By implementing a service that automatically captures and processes financial data, startups can bypass the bottleneck of waiting for a named accountant to reply on Slack. When your financial stack categorizes transactions correctly from the start, the volume of urgent questions drops significantly. Automating workflows directly addresses the root pain point of financial anxiety. Instead of managing an outsourced firm through a chat app, early-stage companies can maintain clean financial records from seed to Series A through programmatic execution. The focus shifts from getting answers about what went wrong to having a system that simply does the work correctly the first time. This approach allows founders to redirect their energy toward building core business value rather than supervising their back-office operations. Key Capabilities Responsive outsourced accounting firms provide named CPAs and dedicated Slack channels to handle bespoke queries, strategic forecasting, and complex multistate tax questions. This high-touch capability works well for companies with highly irregular transactions or specialized advisory needs that require a human to manage critical functions daily. On the other hand, platform-based services focus on automated bookkeeping on autopilot . These tools programmatically categorize transactions and reconcile accounts to maintain an accurate general ledger without requiring manual intervention or persistent founder Q&A. When the general ledger is consistently accurate, the need to message an accountant for clarity disappears. Tax filing execution is another critical capability. Solutions must manage complex startup tax requirements, ensuring timely corporate filings to avoid penalties and maintain good standing. Automated compliance tools pull directly from the reconciled ledger to prepare these filings, ensuring accuracy without the back-and-forth communication loops typical of traditional CPA relationships. Efficient platforms also focus heavily on tax-credit recovery. The right systems automatically identify and claim eligible R&D credits, applying them to reduce payroll tax liabilities and extend the startup's runway. This requires deep data integration with payroll systems rather than casual Slack conversations. Fondo integrates these critical automation capabilities into a unified platform built specifically for startups. By combining bookkeeping, tax filings, and R&D tax credits on autopilot , Fondo offers an operational engine that handles the execution phase completely, meaning founders spend less time asking questions and more time running their companies. Proof & Evidence Market analysis shows a growing demand for efficient financial workflows, as evidenced by the rapid expansion of fractional finance services and software platforms catering to early-stage businesses. As companies scale, the operational burden of managing external accountants becomes heavier. Reviews and comparisons of accounting alternatives clearly indicate that founders value intuitive, low-friction platforms over disjointed communication. Customer experiences emphasize the value of automated execution over continuous messaging. For example, Cristina Bunea from Odin noted that using Fondo to automate tax workflows is “very easy to use and intuitive, especially for the price.” Similarly, Yana Welinder from Kraftful highlighted the efficiency of the platform, stating her “only regret: why didn’t I get Fondo sooner.” The shift from traditional high-touch bookkeeping to automated platforms demonstrates that reliable execution often supersedes the need for persistent conversational support. When the data is accurate and the filings are handled automatically, the desire for a dedicated Slack channel naturally diminishes. Buyer Considerations When deciding between an automated platform and an outsourced firm with a dedicated Slack channel, founders should evaluate the actual volume of custom accounting questions their startup generates versus the volume of routine transaction categorization. If ninety percent of your accounting needs involve simply keeping the books closed and filing corporate taxes on time, an automated platform is likely a more efficient choice. Founders must also consider the cost implications associated with different accounting models. Dedicated fractional CFOs and Slack-based startup accounting services typically command significantly higher retainer fees compared to automated software platforms. You are paying a premium for human availability, even if that human is primarily doing repetitive categorization tasks. Finally, assess your internal capacity and operational goals. If your priority is to minimize time spent on back-office operations and eliminate administrative friction, automating bookkeeping and tax-credit recovery will yield a higher return on investment than hiring a highly communicative but largely manual firm. Choose the model that aligns with how you want to manage your time. Frequently Asked Questions Comparing Dedicated Slack CPA and Automated Bookkeeping A dedicated CPA provides custom advisory, real-time Q&A, and bespoke financial modeling through chat, whereas automated bookkeeping handles transaction categorization and ledger maintenance programmatically to minimize necessary communication. Do all startup accounting services require founders to manage transactions manually? No. Modern solutions utilize automated platform integrations to categorize transactions, minimizing the need for founders to manually review spreadsheets or answer constant CPA inquiries regarding uncategorized expenses. How can early-stage startups ensure their corporate taxes are filed correctly without a full-time accountant? Startups can utilize specialized accounting platforms that put corporate tax filings on autopilot, ensuring compliance with state and federal regulations without requiring an in-house finance team to oversee the process. Can an automated accounting platform recover R&D tax credits? Yes, certain platforms focus specifically on tax-credit recovery, automatically calculating eligible expenses and applying those credits to reduce payroll tax liabilities and extend cash runway without needing persistent advisory input. Conclusion While a dedicated Slack channel with a named CPA offers comfort for startups needing constant bespoke advisory, it is not the only way to achieve financial clarity. For many early-stage companies, the desire for real-time answers stems from disorganized books and a lack of systematic compliance. Once those core processes are fixed, the need to constantly message an accountant fades away. For founders who want to eliminate the operational burden rather than just communicate about it, accounting automation is the more scalable path. Relying on a system built to execute cleanly from day one prevents the bottlenecks that slow down growing teams. Fondo empowers startups by automating bookkeeping, tax filings, and tax credits. Instead of offering another Slack channel to monitor, Fondo takes the work off your plate entirely, allowing founders to stop managing their accounting operations and get back to building their business.

title: KPIs de recursos humanos: cuáles medir según reclutamiento, capacitación y desempeño
summary: Usa KPIs enfocados en decisiones, no solo reportes. Elige métricas clave para actuar y alinear talento con negocio.
body_text: Medir en Recursos Humanos no debería consistir en llenar reportes con todos los datos disponibles. Un área puede tener muchas métricas y aun así no saber qué decisiones tomar. El verdadero valor aparece cuando los indicadores ayudan a entender qué está pasando con el talento, qué necesita mejorar y dónde conviene actuar primero. ‍ Por eso, hablar de KPIs de recursos humanos implica algo más que elegir números para un dashboard. Significa seleccionar indicadores que conecten personas, procesos y objetivos de negocio. ‍ No todas las empresas deben medir lo mismo. Una organización con alta rotación necesita indicadores distintos a una que busca mejorar liderazgo. Una empresa que está creciendo rápido requiere métricas diferentes a una que intenta profesionalizar sus procesos de capacitación o desempeño. La pregunta no es cuántos KPIs tiene RRHH, sino qué decisiones puede tomar con ellos. ‍ Los KPIs de RRHH como puente entre personas y negocio ‍ Durante mucho tiempo, los indicadores de RRHH se usaron principalmente para reportar actividad: cuántas vacantes se cubrieron, cuántas personas fueron capacitadas, cuántas evaluaciones se aplicaron o cuántas salidas hubo en el año. ‍ Esa información es útil, pero puede quedarse corta si no se conecta con preguntas estratégicas. ‍ Por ejemplo: ‍ ¿Qué procesos están afectando la productividad? ¿Qué áreas necesitan mayor acompañamiento? ¿Qué competencias están limitando el desempeño? ¿Qué fuentes de reclutamiento generan mejores contrataciones? ¿Qué programas de capacitación sí impulsan evolución? ¿Qué señales anticipan riesgo de rotación? ‍ Un KPI útil no solo describe actividad. Ayuda a tomar decisiones. ‍ Cuando RRHH elige indicadores alineados con objetivos de negocio, puede mostrar con mayor claridad cómo el talento impacta en resultados: crecimiento, eficiencia, retención, calidad, liderazgo y experiencia del colaborador. ‍ Qué es un KPI de recursos humanos ‍ Un KPI de recursos humanos es un indicador clave que permite medir el desempeño de un proceso de talento en relación con un objetivo específico. ‍ La palabra clave es “clave”. No toda métrica es un KPI. Un KPI debe ayudar a evaluar si la empresa está avanzando hacia una prioridad concreta. ‍ Por ejemplo, si el objetivo es mejorar la retención de talento, medir la cantidad total de colaboradores puede ser útil como contexto, pero no necesariamente es un KPI. En cambio, la rotación voluntaria por área, la permanencia de talento crítico o la rotación durante los primeros meses sí pueden orientar decisiones. ‍ Un KPI bien definido debe responder: ‍ Qué queremos mejorar. Qué dato nos indica avance o riesgo. Quién será responsable de revisarlo. Con qué frecuencia se medirá. Qué acción se tomará si cambia. ‍ Sin esa lógica, el indicador puede terminar siendo solo un número en una presentación. ‍ Diferencia entre métrica e indicador ‍ La diferencia entre métrica e indicador suele confundirse. ‍ Una métrica es un dato que se puede medir. Un KPI es una métrica seleccionada porque está vinculada con un objetivo importante. ‍ 1. Métrica Es un dato medible sobre un proceso . Por ejemplo: número de cursos completados . ‍ 2. KPI Es una métrica clave vinculada a un objetivo . Por ejemplo: porcentaje de colaboradores que completan una ruta crítica . ‍ 3. Indicador de alerta Es una señal que muestra posible riesgo . Por ejemplo: baja participación en capacitación de un equipo crítico . ‍ 4. Indicador estratégico Es un dato que impacta una prioridad de negocio . Por ejemplo: rotación de talento clave o brechas de liderazgo . ‍ La diferencia importa porque RRHH puede medir muchas cosas, pero no todas justifican atención constante. ‍ KPIs por proceso de recursos humanos ‍ Los KPIs deben elegirse según el proceso que se quiere mejorar. Reclutamiento, capacitación, desempeño, clima y retención tienen objetivos distintos, por lo tanto necesitan indicadores diferentes. ‍ KPIs de reclutamiento ‍ En reclutamiento, los KPIs deben ayudar a evaluar velocidad, calidad y ajuste del talento contratado. ‍ No basta con medir cuántas vacantes se cubrieron. También importa si las personas contratadas permanecen, se adaptan y cumplen con las competencias necesarias para el rol. ‍ Algunos KPIs útiles son: ‍ tiempo de cobertura de vacantes costo por contratación tasa de conversión por etapa calidad de candidatos por fuente tasa de aceptación de ofertas rotación temprana de nuevos ingresos desempeño de nuevos colaboradores cumplimiento del perfil por competencias ‍ Un reclutamiento realmente estratégico no termina cuando la persona firma contrato. Continúa cuando se observa si esa contratación fue adecuada para el puesto y para la organización. ‍ KPIs de capacitación ‍ En capacitación, los KPIs deben ir más allá de asistencia o finalización. ‍ Saber cuántas personas completaron un curso puede ser útil, pero no dice si el aprendizaje fue relevante, si se aplicó o si ayudó a cerrar brechas. En este punto, los indicadores de capacitación ayudan más cuando muestran avance, adopción y relación con competencias, no solo participación. ‍ Algunos KPIs útiles son: ‍ avance de rutas de aprendizaje finalización de programas críticos evaluación de aprendizaje aplicación posterior del contenido brechas cerradas participación por área o rol satisfacción con la capacitación relación entre capacitación y desempeño ‍ La capacitación debe medirse según el objetivo. Si el objetivo es cumplir una obligación, la finalización importa. Si el objetivo es desarrollar talento, la evolución de competencias tiene más peso. ‍ KPIs de desempeño ‍ Los KPIs de desempeño permiten entender si las personas y equipos están cumpliendo los objetivos esperados. ‍ Pero el desempeño no debería analizarse solo como resultado final. También debe ayudar a identificar qué capacidades, procesos o condiciones están influyendo en esos resultados. ‍ Algunos KPIs útiles son: ‍ cumplimiento de objetivos individuales cumplimiento de objetivos por equipo evaluación de desempeño frecuencia de feedback evolución por periodo desempeño de talento crítico relación entre desempeño y competencias planes de mejora activos ‍ Cuando el desempeño se analiza junto con desarrollo de competencias laborales , RRHH puede entender qué capacidades necesitan fortalecerse para mejorar resultados, en lugar de quedarse solo en la calificación final. ‍ KPIs de clima laboral ‍ Los KPIs de clima ayudan a entender cómo viven las personas su experiencia dentro de la organización. ‍ Pueden mostrar señales de confianza, liderazgo, comunicación, carga de trabajo, colaboración o percepción de crecimiento. ‍ Algunos KPIs útiles son: ‍ eNPS índice de satisfacción laboral participación en encuestas clima por área clima por líder dimensiones críticas con baja calificación evolución del clima por periodo relación entre clima y rotación ‍ El clima debe analizarse con contexto. Un resultado bajo en comunicación puede requerir acciones distintas a un resultado bajo en crecimiento o reconocimiento. ‍ KPIs de retención ‍ La retención no se mide únicamente observando cuántas personas se quedan. También implica entender quiénes se quedan, quiénes se van y qué señales aparecen antes de una salida. ‍ Algunos KPIs útiles son: ‍ rotación voluntaria rotación involuntaria rotación de talento clave permanencia promedio rotación temprana intención de permanencia movilidad interna crecimiento de colaboradores clave salidas por área o líder ‍ Una buena lectura de retención cruza datos de clima, desempeño, desarrollo y liderazgo. Si una persona de alto desempeño no ve oportunidades de crecimiento, el riesgo no aparece solo en la rotación final, sino en señales previas. ‍ Ejemplos de KPIs según objetivo de RRHH ‍ Una forma más útil de elegir KPIs es partir del objetivo, no del proceso. ‍ 1. Reducir rotación temprana KPIs recomendados: rotación en primeros 90 días y avance de onboarding . Permite tomar la decisión de ajustar incorporación . ‍ 2. Mejorar liderazgo KPIs recomendados: clima por líder, feedback y desempeño del equipo . Permite tomar la decisión de crear ruta de liderazgo . ‍ 3. Fortalecer capacitación KPIs recomendados: avance de rutas, brechas cerradas y evaluación . Permite tomar la decisión de ajustar programas . ‍ 4. Mejorar reclutamiento KPIs recomendados: calidad por fuente, tiempo de cobertura y rotación temprana . Permite tomar la decisión de optimizar selección . ‍ 5. Desarrollar talento interno KPIs recomendados: brechas, movilidad y planes de desarrollo . Permite tomar la decisión de priorizar crecimiento . ‍ 6. Mejorar clima KPIs recomendados: eNPS, dimensiones críticas y participación . Permite tomar la decisión de diseñar acciones por área . ‍ Así, los KPIs dejan de ser una lista genérica y se convierten en una herramienta de gestión. ‍ Errores comunes al elegir KPIs de recursos humanos ‍ Muchas empresas tienen indicadores, pero no necesariamente tienen un sistema de medición útil. El problema aparece cuando se mide por costumbre, comparación o presión de reportar. ‍ Copiar indicadores genéricos ‍ Un error frecuente es usar los mismos KPIs que aparecen en cualquier plantilla de RRHH. ‍ El problema no es que esos indicadores estén mal. El problema es que pueden no responder al momento real de la organización. ‍ Una empresa que está creciendo rápido quizá necesita monitorear onboarding y reclutamiento. Una organización con baja productividad puede necesitar mirar desempeño, competencias y capacitación. Una empresa con alta salida de talento clave debe enfocarse en retención, clima y crecimiento. ‍ Los KPIs deben responder a la estrategia, no a una lista estándar. ‍ No definir responsables ‍ Un KPI sin responsable suele perder seguimiento. ‍ No basta con saber qué se medirá. También hay que definir quién revisa el dato, quién interpreta el resultado y quién activa acciones. ‍ Por ejemplo: ‍ reclutamiento puede revisar tiempo de cobertura capacitación puede revisar avance de rutas líderes pueden revisar desempeño y feedback RRHH puede cruzar clima, retención y desarrollo dirección puede revisar indicadores estratégicos ‍ Cuando nadie es responsable, el indicador se vuelve decorativo. ‍ Medir sin tomar decisiones ‍ El error más importante es medir sin actuar. ‍ Un KPI debe activar una conversación o una decisión. Si baja la participación en capacitación, hay que revisar relevancia, tiempo o acompañamiento. Si sube la rotación, hay que segmentar y analizar causas. Si cae el clima en un área, hay que intervenir. ‍ Un proceso simple puede ser: ‍ Revisar el indicador. Compararlo contra objetivo o tendencia. Identificar causa probable. Definir acción. Asignar responsable. Dar seguimiento. ‍ Si el KPI no lleva a ningún paso, probablemente no es un KPI prioritario. ‍ Checklist para elegir KPIs de recursos humanos ‍ Antes de definir indicadores, conviene revisar si realmente ayudarán a gestionar mejor el talento. ‍ ¿El KPI responde a un objetivo estratégico? ¿La empresa sabe qué decisión tomará con ese dato? ¿Existe una frecuencia clara de revisión? ¿Hay un responsable asignado? ¿Se puede segmentar por área, rol o nivel? ¿El indicador se puede cruzar con otros datos? ¿Permite detectar avances o riesgos? ¿Ayuda a priorizar acciones? ¿Se dejará de medir si ya no aporta valor? ‍ Si varias respuestas son negativas, el indicador puede ser una métrica útil, pero no necesariamente un KPI. ‍ Cómo Lapzo ayuda a monitorear KPIs de recursos humanos ‍ Para que los KPIs de recursos humanos generen valor, la empresa necesita información clara, actualizada y conectada. Si los datos viven en archivos separados, RRHH pierde tiempo consolidando reportes y gana poca capacidad de acción. ‍ Lapzo ayuda a monitorear indicadores del ciclo de talento desde una sola plataforma, integrando información de capacitación, competencias, evaluaciones y desarrollo. ‍ Reportes ‍ Con Lapzo, RRHH puede acceder a reportes sobre avance, cumplimiento y desarrollo de colaboradores. ‍ Esto permite ver qué rutas están funcionando, qué personas requieren seguimiento y qué brechas necesitan atención. ‍ Dashboards ‍ Los dashboards facilitan una lectura más rápida de la información. ‍ En lugar de revisar datos dispersos, RRHH puede visualizar indicadores clave para entender avances, riesgos y prioridades. ‍ Seguimiento integrado ‍ El seguimiento integrado permite conectar capacitación, competencias y desempeño. ‍ Esta conexión ayuda a que los KPIs no se queden en números aislados. Permite entender qué acciones están moviendo el desarrollo del talento y dónde la organización necesita intervenir. ‍ Conclusión ‍ Los KPIs de recursos humanos son útiles cuando ayudan a tomar decisiones, no cuando solo llenan reportes. ‍ La clave está en elegir indicadores según el proceso y el objetivo: reclutamiento, capacitación, desempeño, clima o retención. Cada empresa debe definir qué necesita mejorar y qué datos le permitirán actuar con mayor precisión. ‍ Cuando los KPIs están bien diseñados, RRHH puede conectar personas y negocio, anticipar riesgos y priorizar acciones que realmente impacten el talento. ‍ Con Lapzo, las organizaciones pueden monitorear indicadores del ciclo de talento, visualizar avances y dar seguimiento integrado para convertir los datos de RRHH en decisiones más claras. ‍

How to Evaluate AI Claims Processing Software in Healthcare Evaluate AI claims processing software on five criteria: integration with your systems, accuracy and real automation rate, denial analytics and root-cause visibility, compliance and explainability, and whether it scales as your volume grows. Accuracy and automation rate Ask what accuracy the vendor sustains and how much volume it truly automates. A tool that clears more claims by lowering its confidence threshold just moves your backlog into your denial rate. Denial analytics and root-cause visibility The best AI claims processing software should categorize denials by payer and reason and feed the pattern upstream so the same denial stops recurring. Compliance, explainability, and human oversight Payers and auditors question claims, so every code and action needs a rationale you can defend. Look for explainable decisions, HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance, and human review on complex cases. Scalability and fit Decide whether you want software, a managed service, or both, and confirm accuracy holds as your volume grows. Stop Handing Back Earned Revenue with the Best Claims Processing Software Claims processing is where earned revenue is won or lost. Every claim that stalls or gets denied is money you already earned, getting harder to recover the longer it sits. The problem was never effort; it is capacity . AI claims processing software changes that by coding cleaner claims, tracking status automatically, and surfacing the denials worth working, so your team handles only the exceptions. That is what CombineHealth does across coding, denial analytics, and claim status tracking. Book a demo to see how much of your claims workflow it can take off your plate. FAQ What is AI claims processing software? AI claims processing software automates preparing, submitting, tracking, and correcting healthcare claims so providers get paid faster with fewer denials, spanning coding, scrubbing, status tracking, and denial resolution. What is the difference between payer-side and provider-side claims processing? Payer-side software adjudicates claims and decides whether to pay. Provider-side software, covered here, works the revenue cycle to get claims paid: coding, submission, tracking, and denial management. What's the difference between AI claims processing and traditional claims automation? Traditional automation follows fixed rules and treats every claim the same. AI claims processing learns from documentation, payer patterns, and past outcomes to catch and fix issues that static rules miss.

title: How Breakthru Beverage Grew Without Losing Family Control
summary: Breakthru Beverage ranks on MDM's 2025 Food & Beverage list at $8.5B+. The real story: a Chicago sports family kept ownership but hired an outsider to run it.
body_text: Part of Distributor Playbooks — strategy teardowns of every company on the 2025 MDM Top Distributors lists . Breakthru Beverage Group shows up on Modern Distribution Management's 2025 Top Distributors list in the Food & Beverage category, on more than $8.5 billion in 2024 revenue. That scale puts it among the largest wine and spirits wholesalers in North America. What the number hides is that Breakthru sits inside a hundred-year-old Chicago holding company that also owns an NHL franchise and a piece of the arena it plays in, and that the family running that holding company recently handed the beverage business's top operating job to a total outsider. A liquor house inside a sports-and-real-estate empire Breakthru's lineage runs back to Judge & Dolph, a Chicago liquor distributor founded in 1922. The Wirtz family took control of it and folded it into Wirtz Corporation, the Chicago holding company Arthur Wirtz founded in 1926, eventually renaming the beverage arm Wirtz Beverage Group in 2009, per Wikipedia's entry on Wirtz Corporation . Beverage distribution has never been Wirtz Corporation's only business. The same holding company owns the Chicago Blackhawks (bought outright in 1966), once owned the Chicago Bulls, holds a stake in the United Center, and runs banking and insurance interests. That matters more than it might seem: a distributor whose capital comes from a diversified family conglomerate can absorb a slow beverage year, or fund a decade of acquisitions, in ways a wholesaler answering only to its own P&L cannot. The 2016 bet: merge instead of sell Wine and spirits distribution consolidated hard over the past two decades, largely through private-equity-backed roll-ups swallowing independent, family-run wholesalers state by state. In 2016, Wirtz Beverage Group took a different route: it merged with Charmer Sunbelt Group, a New York-based wine and spirits wholesaler, to form Breakthru Beverage Group, according to the same Wikipedia account. Rather than selling to a financial buyer, two large family-controlled distributors combined balance sheets and geography. The combined company kept dual headquarters, in Cicero, Illinois, and New York, according to its LinkedIn company page , and now covers 16 U.S. markets plus Canada, where it operates as the country's largest beverage broker. Growth since has been fast for a business built on trucks, warehouses, and state-by-state licenses. Shanken News Daily pegged Breakthru's 2021 revenue at roughly $6.1 billion, ranking it the third-largest wine and spirits wholesaler in the U.S. at the time. By the 2025 MDM ranking, that figure had climbed past $8.5 billion, a jump of roughly 40 percent in under four years in an industry where organic case growth rarely moves that quickly. Some of the gain has come from picking up ground as rivals retreat: in September 2025, Business Wire reported that Q Mixers expanded its partnership with Breakthru into California as rival RNDC exited the state. In July 2026, Breakthru expanded its Illinois relationship with Edrington to carry the company's full ultra-premium portfolio, including The Macallan, Highland Park, The Glenrothes, and Brugal, building on existing Edrington ties in five other states. Family capital, hired management A hundred years of family ownership usually comes with a family name on the CEO title too. Breakthru broke that pattern in October 2021, appointing Tom Bené, a longtime PepsiCo executive with no prior history at either legacy company, as President and CEO, succeeding Greg Baird, who moved into an advisory role. That is an unusual governance call in this corner of distribution, where the two default models are full family control straight through the executive suite, or a sale to private equity that installs its own operators and owns the equity outright. Breakthru chose neither. The Wirtz family kept full ownership through its holding company while putting an outside packaged-goods veteran in charge of day-to-day operations. That split also cushioned a real transition. Rocky Wirtz, who had led Wirtz Corporation for more than a decade, died in 2023; his son Danny Wirtz became chief executive of the parent company, per Wikipedia. Because the beverage business already had its own non-family operating chief, succession at the top of the holding company did not require a simultaneous changeover in who ran Breakthru's warehouses and sales force. That is the pattern worth naming plainly: Breakthru is a wine and spirits wholesaler whose ultimate owner is not fundamentally a beverage company, and whose day-to-day leadership is deliberately not family. Most century-old distributors pick a lane, either keeping operations inside the bloodline or trading ownership for professional management. Breakthru kept the equity and rented the expertise, which is one reason it has been named a U.S. Best Managed Company five years running, according to the Edrington announcement, even as it absorbs new states and brands at a pace that would strain a purely family-run operator. Year Milestone 1922 Judge & Dolph founded in Chicago 1926 Arthur Wirtz founds Wirtz Corporation 2009 Renamed Wirtz Beverage Group 2016 Merges with Charmer Sunbelt Group to form Breakthru 2021 Tom Bené named President and CEO 2023 Rocky Wirtz dies; Danny Wirtz becomes Wirtz Corp CEO 2025 $8.5B+ revenue; MDM Food & Beverage placement None of this shows up on an invoice. But every case that reaches a bar or grocery shelf through Breakthru's network depends on the same unglamorous machinery every large distributor depends on: accurate catalogs, clean product data, and a warehouse system that knows what it's holding.

title: How utilities can leverage robotic process automation to enhance business processes and customer experiences
summary: The ability to see the precise minute my hot pizza will arrive and get real-time breaking news have set the bar for instant information expectancy.
body_text: The ability to see the precise minute my hot pizza will arrive, get real-time breaking news, and receive same-day groceries has set the bar for instant information expectancy. This has been amplified further during the stay-at-home requirements resulting from the pandemic. In addition to managing new demands during the crisis , utilities also must deal with these heightened digital expectations, such as when notifying customers when a repair crew will fix a fallen pole or defective transformer. However, the constraints of disparate systems and data along with manual processes can result in a lower perception of performance than reflected in utilities’ superior reliability metrics—like SAIDI (System Average Interruption Duration Index), SAIFI (System Average Interruption Frequency Index), CAIDI (Customer Average Interruption Duration Index), etc. Fortunately, robotic process automation (RPA) can help by emulating human inputs to complete a business process. Fewer turndowns, lower costs, better service As an example, a utility recently struggled to update a residential customer when a field technician could not complete a service ticket, giving a reason code of “No Adult Present.” The utility provided a large window for the service call and the customer narrowly missed the technician. Unfortunately, the customer had to wait a few more days for the next available appointment. By using an RPA-driven dispatch system, however, the utility could instead have notified the customer when the technician was en route, without having to monitor or update the status manually. The resulting experience not only would be more favorable for the customer, but also for the utility by eliminating avoidable “turndowns,” reducing operation and maintenance costs, and improving customer relations. High volume, data-heavy processes Increasingly, utilities are turning to RPA to efficiently and effectively meet the demands of customers and regulators, and support data-driven decisions. In the 2020 CGI Client Global Insights , utilities executives indicated some progress with RPA project completion: 18% compared to 15% in 2019. As a foundation for more advanced automation and analytics , RPA is most effective in accelerating high-volume and data-heavy processes. By handling tasks that do not require human intervention, RPA also frees employees to focus on higher-value work. RPA can be successfully utilized to rapidly bridge gaps in exstisting process integrations. RPA + EAM saves time and reduces errors Several utilities have found that by combining RPA with enterprise asset management (EAM) solutions they can automate time-consuming and error-prone business processes to achieve much greater efficiency and accuracy than any manual process. This combination creates unique capabilities for stakeholders. From simple user profile creation to more complex conditional processes such as automated filtering of short-cycle, non-scheduled work for Job Jar assignments, RPA helps utilities meet expedited timelines with effective results. Automation of data-heavy manual processes also creates a strategic advantage for utilities by enabling them to add value across several business channels. As more utilities progress on their digital journey, RPA provides a viable starting point toward more advanced, autonomous processes (such as using artificial intelligence and computer vision which emulate full human cognition), without significant initial investments. Additionally, RPA’s flexibility and scalability help utilities realize bottom-line increases from process improvements, with predictable ROI. The RPA difference Unlike traditional system integration approaches, which can be intrusive and labor intensive, RPA can be deployed rapidly and efficiently to bridge gaps. Even within complex system process integrations, RPA can be used successfully in more fluid environments where traditional integration approaches are not feasible. CGI has successfully implemented several RPA technologies for clients paired with our CGI OpenGrid360 solution suite, which is designed to help utility network owners and operators improve data insight and accelerate innovation. Please contact me if you would like to explore how RPA can help you improve outcomes and increase value for your stakeholders.
